title: Cook, Levin, and Karp: The Birth of NP-Completeness (1971-72)
explainer: In 1971 Stephen Cook proved that Boolean satisfiability (SAT) is NP-complete, showing every problem in NP can be reduced to it in polynomial time; Leonid Levin independently proved the same result in the Soviet Union around the same time, which is why it is called the Cook-Levin theorem. Richard Karp's 1972 paper then showed that 21 other practical problems were also NP-complete, turning the idea from an isolated curiosity into the organizing framework behind the hardness results this lesson covers.

resources.title: Lecture 15: NP-Completeness (18.404J Theory of Computation, Fall 2020)

title: Christofides and the Approximation-Algorithms Tradition (1976)
explainer: When a problem is NP-hard, one practical response is to accept a provably good approximate answer instead of an exact one. Nicos Christofides' 1976 algorithm for the metric traveling salesman problem guarantees a tour no more than 1.5 times the optimal length, and for the general problem that worst-case guarantee went essentially unbeaten for decades - a concrete historical illustration of the approximation-ratio thinking this lesson introduces.
